worker_input_rule: Only exact files inside selected cases/<id>. Exclude manifest, cohort README, oracle, case IDs, other cases, and evaluator results. Enforce isolation separately.
oracle_policy: Only stdlib execution of trusted freshly authored source. Seven evaluator checks, one expected failure for q1 plus a separate positive witness. Public baselines pass. Never attribute evaluator execution to audit workers.
limitations: Three small synthetic cases support local calibration only, not population estimates or real-world effectiveness claims.
Independent authorship is role separation, not evidence of unseen/pretraining novelty.
Oracle expectations are nonexhaustive; novel supported claims need independent review.
Hashes and copied paths do not enforce isolation or establish host compliance.

expected_outcomes: A failed first publish can leave a complete generation without CURRENT. read() still returns None until reopening.

Startup recover() promotes the newest complete generation when CURRENT is absent. A generation that never reached os.replace commitment becomes visible, violating the explicit empty-state recovery contract.

The public failure test begins with an existing commit; its CURRENT early return misses failed first publication. Preserve marker absence as empty or require separate durable commit evidence, and add that boundary check.
accepted_alternatives: Any equivalent supported explanation of uncommitted data promotion after interrupted first publication.
A narrow supported test-gap observation earns partial credit but does not fully identify the consequence.
A proposed deterministic fault-injection check is valid without execution; runtime reproduction requires actual authorized execution evidence.
reject_or_qualify: Do not claim failed updates overwrite an existing committed artifact: recover returns early when CURRENT exists.
Do not invent excluded concurrent-access, power-loss durability, externally corrupt directories, or garbage-collection obligations.
The documented diagnostic listing of uncommitted complete generations is not itself the defect.

oracle.scenario: Start empty; fail os.replace while publishing fixed bytes; restore replacement; reopen.
oracle.contract_expected: None before and after reopening; no committed CURRENT.
oracle.snapshot_observed: None before reopen; candidate bytes and CURRENT generation 1 after reopen.

expected_outcomes: Completed keys identify an operation for the whole bounded batch. Replaying an equal payload preserves the same completed job and result, rather than requesting requeue.
Conflicting payloads under one key are rejected; another key creates another operation.
Fresh tokens fence expired workers even under the same owner name; deadline equality is expired.
A scoped no-finding answer is appropriate.
accepted_alternatives: No findings, with or without discussing intentional completed-key retention.
A limitation framed within the documented bounded, serialized, in-memory scope may be useful.
A novel consequential finding can be accepted after independent contract-grounded verification; this oracle is nonexhaustive.
reject_or_qualify: Completed-key retention is not a requeue defect or an unbounded-service memory leak under the declared single-batch lifecycle.
Do not claim stale completion succeeds without accounting for token and deadline checks.
Persistence and cross-process locking are explicitly outside scope.

oracle.scenario: Complete, replay same key, then enqueue a distinct key; separately expire and reissue a lease under the same owner name.
oracle.contract_expected: Replay keeps completed result and yields no lease; new key is leasable; stale token rejected, fresh token accepted.

expected_outcomes: begin() freezes the upper revision; resume preserves it; a later pull includes writes appended between pages.
Repeated updates and tombstones remain ordered events; detached values protect retained history.
Compaction explicitly expires positions below the inclusive floor, including active continuations; the floor remains usable.
A scoped no-finding answer is appropriate. Adapter snapshot endpoint, token transport, persistence, and multiwriter handling are expressly outside scope.
accepted_alternatives: No findings, without claiming global correctness.
A narrow adapter-integration question is acceptable when explicitly unresolved rather than asserted as a component defect.
Novel material findings can be accepted after independent verification; no planted defect is not a correctness certificate.
reject_or_qualify: Displayed checkpoints do not authorize persisting them before the final page.
Between-page appends are beyond the frozen checkpoint and appear on the next pull; they are not silently lost.
Do not invent snapshot retention or hostile-input promises for invalidated continuations or trusted in-process tokens.

oracle.scenario: Pull revisions 1..3 in single-event pages; append revision 4 between pages; separately compact beyond an active continuation.
oracle.contract_expected: First pull contains 1..3 at checkpoint 3; next pull includes 4. Compacted continuation raises CursorExpired; floor cursor remains valid.
